title: When the Parting Bosom Bleeds
description: When the Parting Bosom Bleeds in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 571, “Prayer for the Sailor”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: When the part-ing bo-som bleeds, When their na-tive shore re-cedes, When the wild and faith-less main Takes them to her trust a-gain, Fa-ther! view the sai-lor's woe Guide them whe-re-soe'er they go.

lines: When the wild and faithless main
Takes them to her trust again,
When the lonely watch they keep,
Bear them daily on their course,
O'er the ocean's breast doth play,
No sweet church-bell warns to prayer,
Thou who on the whelming wave
Thou canst hear them when they pray, —

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
